sites.name: Site01 Connecting ridge (Barker 2021 RoI 4)
sites.subtitle: PGDA Site01 · Barker 2021 RoI 4
sites.description: A ridge at the Moon's south pole, about 17 km from the pole, connecting the rims of Shackleton crater and de Gerlache crater (Barker et al. 2021). Because it is high and close to the pole, where the Sun always stays near the horizon, parts of it see the Sun most of the time: Mazarico et al. (2011) ranked it first of the south polar sites for average illumination (their site 1), and Barker et al. (2021) studied it as a potential landing site. They found seven regions on it where, at 1 m above the ground in 2024-2025, more than 70% of the Sun's disc is in view on average. The point used here is the centre of the largest, region 4.
sites.source: Barker, M. K., et al. (2021), Planet. Space Sci. 203, 105119, doi:10.1016/j.pss.2020.105119, Table 2: centroid of Site01 region of interest 4, polar stereographic x = -11.2875 km, y = -12.1675 km (89.452675 S, 222.851347 E), in the PGDA product 78 Site01 DEM tile. Site01 (Connecting ridge) is site 1 of Mazarico, E., et al. (2011), Icarus 211, 1066-1081, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030.

sites.name: Site04 Shackleton rim (Barker 2021 RoI 1)
sites.subtitle: PGDA Site04 · Barker 2021 RoI 1
sites.description: A point on the rim of Shackleton crater, about 7 km from the Moon's south pole. Mazarico et al. (2011) ranked the south polar sites by average illumination; this is their site 4. Barker et al. (2021) mapped it at 5 m as a potential landing site and outlined four regions on it where, at 1 m above the ground in 2024-2025, more than 70% of the Sun's disc is in view on average. The point used here is the centre of the largest, region 1.
sites.source: Centroid of region of interest 1 (the largest, 279 pixels = 6,975 m2) in Barker et al. (2021)'s Site04_ROIs.tgz (PGDA product 78; Barker, M. K., et al. (2021), Planet. Space Sci. 203, 105119, doi:10.1016/j.pss.2020.105119): polar stereographic x = -2.8125 km, y = -6.6475 km: the centre of the 5 m pixel containing the mean of the region's pixel centres (the rule that reproduces Barker's Table 2 centroids at Site01). Site 4 of Mazarico, E., et al. (2011), Icarus 211, 1066-1081, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030.

sites.name: Site07 Peak near Shackleton (Barker 2021 RoI 2)
sites.subtitle: PGDA Site07 · Barker 2021 RoI 2
sites.description: An isolated peak near Shackleton crater, on the Moon's far side, about 36 km from the south pole (Barker et al. 2021). Mazarico et al. (2011) ranked the south polar sites by average illumination; this is their site 7. Barker et al. (2021) mapped it at 5 m as a potential landing site and outlined two regions on it where, at 1 m above the ground in 2024-2025, more than 70% of the Sun's disc is in view on average. The point used here is the centre of the larger, region 2.
sites.source: Centroid of region of interest 2 (the largest, 662 pixels = 16,550 m2) in Barker et al. (2021)'s Site07_ROIs.tgz (PGDA product 78; Barker, M. K., et al. (2021), Planet. Space Sci. 203, 105119, doi:10.1016/j.pss.2020.105119): polar stereographic x = 30.0625 km, y = -20.1075 km: the centre of the 5 m pixel containing the mean of the region's pixel centres (the rule that reproduces Barker's Table 2 centroids at Site01). Site 7 of Mazarico, E., et al. (2011), Icarus 211, 1066-1081, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030.

sites.name: Site06 Nobile rim 1 (Mazarico 2011 site 6)
sites.subtitle: PGDA Site06 · Mazarico 2011 rank 6
sites.description: A point on the rim of Nobile crater, about 143 km from the Moon's south pole. Mazarico et al. (2011) listed the 50 most illuminated spots near the south pole on a 240 m map; this one ranks 6th, with 86% of the Sun's disc in view on average at surface level over 1970-2044. Barker et al. (2021) made the 5 m map of the site (PGDA product 78) that is used here. The point is Mazarico's published coordinate, given to 0.01 degrees (about 300 m in latitude).
sites.source: Mazarico, E., et al. (2011), Icarus 211, 1066-1081, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030, Table 3 (south pole, rank 6): 37.07 E, 85.30 S (polar stereographic x = 85.958 km, y = 113.780 km on the 1737.4 km sphere). Site name and 5 m map: PGDA product 78 (Barker, M. K., et al. (2021), Planet. Space Sci. 203, 105119, doi:10.1016/j.pss.2020.105119).
